title: A CI red-proof record: verdict-consistency ≠ substantive detection ≠ coverage
prepared_for: Tavares Heath — independent reconstruction test (CUSTOS-CORE red-proof)

propositions.statement: the recorded verdict RED-CONFIRMED follows the declared verdict rule (pytest_exit_code != 0 -> RED-CONFIRMED) applied to the recorded exit code (1)
propositions.basis: From the evidence record v2 (SHA-verified): pytest_exit_code = 1; rule 'observations.pytest_exit_code != 0 -> RED-CONFIRMED; else FAULTY-GREEN'; verdict = RED-CONFIRMED. 1 != 0 => RED-CONFIRMED. This establishes the verdict is CONSISTENT with its own declared rule — an internal-consistency check on the record. It does NOT by itself establish that the underlying run is faithful (P2) or that the substantive regression was detected (P3)

propositions.statement: the recorded non-zero pytest outcome (a test genuinely failed during the run) is corroborated by the preserved execution reports and GitHub's observed workflow behaviour, independently of the record's verdict field
propositions.basis: The pytest output (hash-matched) reads '1 failed, 32 passed' and the JUnit XML (hash-matched) carries tests='33', failures='1' — two views of the SAME run, both the subject's artifacts. The INDEPENDENT corroboration is GitHub's own job steps (not the subject's record): step 7 'Enforce red-proof verdict' (which would exit 1 on a zero exit code) succeeded, and step 9 'Red confirmed' (guarded by exit_code != 0) ran rather than being skipped — so exit_code != 0 on GitHub's own record. These step outcomes are GitHub-hosted execution metadata, recorded SEPARATELY from the subject-generated evidence artifact but DEPENDENT on the same workflow execution and the values it passes — a second, differently-hosted view, not a fully independent re-measurement. Scope: what is corroborated is that a test FAILED / the outcome was NON-ZERO; the exact value '1' is the record's JSON field and is not separately re-derived

propositions.statement: during run 38446904362 an intended admin-auth assertion failed with exactly the symptom the injected regression produces — an admin endpoint (/v1/audit) no longer requiring authentication
propositions.basis: The single failing test (pytest runs with -x) is tests/test_admin_auth.py::TestAdminEndpointsRequireAuth::test_audit_endpoints_reject_missing_token: 'AssertionError: /v1/audit must require auth, got 200' (assert 200 == 401) — an admin endpoint no longer requiring authentication, which is exactly the effect of disabling token verification. The 32 preceding passing tests support that the suite was operational, but do NOT independently exclude every environment-specific cause of this single failure. The causal chain is kept honest, at three levels: (i) the script was DESIGNED to disable auth — established (it does `sed 's/return verify_token(credentials)/return None/' main.py`, and that target exists at main.py@6ed3cff, lines 122 & 137); (ii) the script RAN — corroborated by GitHub's job step 5 'Apply known-bad sabotage patch' (success), independently of the subject's record; (iii) that this modification CAUSED this specific failure is a strong INFERENCE (matching symptom + the subject-declared red-proof premise that the suite is green on clean code), NOT a byte-level demonstration — no post-injection diff or before/after execution was captured here, and FactNotebook does not re-run. What is ESTABLISHED is the scoped claim in the proposition; full causal proof would be more demanding

propositions.statement: every intended 401/auth regression test failed under the sabotage — the full admin-auth regression class was exercised and detected (the sabotage script's own claim: 'Every 401/auth regression test MUST fail')
propositions.basis: CANNOT ESTABLISH — the workflow runs pytest with -x, so execution STOPPED at the first failing assertion (JUnit: 33 testcases = 32 passed + 1 failed; pytest output: 'stopping after 1 failures'). Exactly ONE intended auth assertion was observed to fail; the remaining auth-regression tests in the class were not run, so the record does not permit establishing that the whole class failed. Reason class: coverage / sufficiency. Addressing it would need a re-run of THIS sabotage (001) WITHOUT -x, so the whole class executes. (The subject's proposed third sabotage class probes a DIFFERENT coverage question — whether believed-untested behaviour is covered — not the coverage of this regression class.) This is the observation-set limit the subject declared

acquisition_boundary.submission_form: one public CI run (38446904362): evidence record v2, JUnit XML, pytest output, workflow, sabotage script, code at the commit — published publicly, FN-retrieved
acquisition_boundary.extraction_instrument: the subject's CI (pytest under a known-bad sabotage patch) — FactNotebook re-reads the preserved artifacts, it does NOT re-run the suite
acquisition_boundary.admission_authority: FactNotebook (proposer). Three steps are kept distinct, and integrity is NOT treated as sufficiency: (1) ACQUISITION + INTEGRITY — the machine artifacts were independently retrieved and SHA-256 verified: the retrieved artifacts match the recorded cryptographic digests; their substantive claims remain subject to independent evaluation; (2) ADMISSION as attributed observations — they are direct, structured records, so no interpretive admission step is needed (no fuzzy candidate to adjudicate); (3) RELEVANCE + SUFFICIENCY per proposition — appraised in the reconstruction itself, never inferred from integrity: an intact, authentically-retrieved artifact can still be insufficient for a given proposition (P4 is CANNOT ESTABLISH precisely because the record, though intact, cannot carry the coverage claim). The one reasoned link (the failing assertion realises the sabotage's declared intent, P3) is grounded in the assertion's own message. Not an independent audit
acquisition_boundary.limitations: Bounded to one run (38446904362, sabotage 001). The evidence record is produced by the subject's own CI, but it was independently retrieved and its JUnit / pytest-output SHA-256 match it, and GitHub's own job-step outcomes corroborate exit != 0 independently of it. The suite was NOT re-run here. Crucially, pytest ran with -x: only the FIRST failing assertion was recorded, so coverage of the full regression class is not observable from this run (P4). This establishes what the preserved record permits — not that CUSTOS-CORE's controls are adequate.
